done.what: Every technique now puts up its result line, because a technique's result belongs to its own record and not to its animation. The original decides it by reading one byte of the technique's record -- the attack category -- and dispatching through a five-row table (docs/research/battle/battle-message-page-kinds-2026-10-04.md section 10); nothing on that path looks at the animation the technique plays, and the animation's strike is only a spark effect. The walker had it the other way round: a technique's line was built inside the moment its animation was struck, so any move whose animation never strikes lost its line completely. Reading all 246 shipped character models found SEVENTEEN such moves, not the seven the first pass reported: the seven field moves and the ten big-attack moves, whose animation is a cinematic whose only effect is a type-66 flash rather than the strike. Four more models ship a strike-less animation for a move that normally strikes. The result is now committed when the move's animation finishes, at the basic attack, the player's technique and the enemy's alike; a strike still commits it early, so nothing that lands on a blow got slower. The heal amount for techniques 184-186 is decoded and ported too: the earlier note called the address a table, and it is one routine that computes the heal from the move's own power and the fighter's WISDOM (power * 64 plus wisdom * power / 8, capped at 9999), and the same arm applies the capped amount to the fighter. LEFT: techniques 187-188 walk three party members instead of one and are not ported; whether a heal move rolls for accuracy at all is not established, so the walker keeps its own roll.

done.state: Correction pass on c163fde1 (the lead rejected three claims; each is re-read line by line in pro/fightstg.s). (1) The heal reads RECORD 400's own power (8), not record 2's (60): `li $a1, 0x190` at :13710 is the delay slot of the branch that reaches the arm, so $a1 is 400 at `jalr` :13999; the `li $a1, 0x2` at :13696 belongs to the 209/210 branch and is spent in the Chi arm's `sllv`. The amount is now 8*64 + WIS = 512 + WIS, capped at 9999 — a plant feeding its ally restores a few hundred points, not four thousand. (2) A lost roll reads `li $v0, 0x2f` in the roll's `beqz` DELAY slot (:13889 / :13907 / :13924), so the branch's own target stores esmfight[0x2f] (:13896 / :13914 / :13931) and kind 1 prints "No effect!" on line one — the empty esmfight[0x00] the previous revision read was the getter's zero return, which the delay slot overwrites. (3) 391's getter is FIGHTSTG_F0x800a13c0, not the body 211/212 share: it walks EIGHT rows of the disc's DIGIMON_PROFILES table (0x8003ef5c, stride 0x58 — `lui $a0, 0x8004` + `addiu $a0, -0x10a4`, NOT 0x80042efc) against the PLAYER's active record `+0x10`, the ATTACK MODIFIER, and returns zero in the `bne`'s delay slots before it ever calls rand — so a blocked cast draws nothing and says "No effect!". The eight profile ids (383, 385, 384, 3, 145, 366, 373, 31) are read out of the committed resident image by the test, not typed. [0x800a4644] = FIGHTSTG_F0x800a1458 is a fourth body and NO category-5 arm loads it. Re-checked on the same rule and also corrected: 392's no-MP refusal is KIND 2 with word 1 = 0x10 (it jumps onto the landed arm's own tail); the one-stat arm's word 1 is the TARGET side * 16, 0 for the player, not the category-2/3 arms' sltiu selector; the party arm's word 0 is the raw acting-side byte, so an enemy Mega Strength now names the enemy's side to kind 9's scan; and the stat writer's lower clamp tests the value it just stored (`slt $v0, $a2` :32299, short form), not the delta, so a second debuff of an already-weakened fighter is floored where it used to pass through. Every correction is proved against c163fde1's own bundle by asking both the same nine questions (.bunny-scratch/old/proof.mjs), and the eight profile ids by reading the disc image.
